<DOCUMENT>
<TYPE>EX-99.1
<SEQUENCE>2
<FILENAME>u10286exv99w1.htm
<DESCRIPTION>EX-99.1
<TEXT>
<HTML>
<HEAD>
<TITLE>exv99w1</TITLE>
</HEAD>
<BODY bgcolor="#FFFFFF">
<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<DIV style="font-family: Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif">

<P><DIV style="position: relative; float: left; width: 5%">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 30pt"><IMG src="u10286u1028600.gif" alt="(RIO TINTO LOGO)">
</DIV>

</DIV>
<DIV style="position: relative; float: right; width: 90%">

<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Exhibit&nbsp;99.1</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">120 Collins Street<BR>
Melbourne 3000<BR>
Australia<BR>
T &#043;61 (0)&nbsp;3 9283 3333<BR>
F &#043;61 (0)&nbsp;3 9283 3707
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt">Press release
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>Rio Tinto gives green light to further US$1.2&nbsp;billion iron ore investment in the next step of Australia&#146;s largest mining project</B>

</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>1 December&nbsp;2010</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto has approved a further US$1.2&nbsp;billion investment in its drive to lift annual
iron ore production capacity in Western Australia&#146;s Pilbara region to 283&nbsp;million tonnes
per annum (Mt/a). The capital will be used for significant expansions at the Brockman 4
and Western Turner Syncline mines.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">This latest development is part of Rio Tinto&#146;s broader plan to expand capacity by more
than 50 per cent over the next five years to 333 Mt/a, which is the largest mining
project in Australian history. Rio Tinto has announced new investment of US$7.2&nbsp;billion
(Rio Tinto share US$5.1&nbsp;billion) in the Pilbara since July this year.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto chief executive Iron Ore and Australia, Sam Walsh said the expanded mines
would provide the bulk of the additional throughput for the recently announced US$3.1
billion rail and port works around Cape Lambert.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&#147;These decisions highlight our strategy of bringing on new capacity in line
with infrastructure developments, using 100 per cent Rio Tinto-owned brownfield
developments to dovetail with existing infrastructure where possible,&#148; he said.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&#147;It also highlights the wealth of large, long-life, well situated and wholly owned
deposits we can bring forward in conjunction with our expansions of port and rail
capacity.&#148;
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Brockman 4 mine (about 60 kilometres west of Tom Price) will be expanded from an
annual capacity of 22&nbsp;million tonnes (Mt/a) to 40 Mt/a. The mine is currently ramping to
reach its first phase capacity in 1H 2011. Only opened in September, within three years it
will become Rio Tinto&#146;s second largest iron ore mine.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Western Turner Syncline mine (about 30 kilometres west of Tom Price) will be
expanded from its current 6 Mt/a capacity to 15 Mt/a.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Both mines are wholly owned by Rio Tinto, and the ore from each deposit will contribute
to Rio Tinto&#146;s Pilbara Blend lump and fines products.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The two projects represent the first two of three mine developments to expand mine capacity
to 283 Mt/a by the fourth quarter of 2013. The third mine earmarked for expansion as part
of this programme, Nammuldi (50 kilometres north west of Tom Price) is currently under
study, with an investment decision expected in 2011.
</DIV>





<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Cont...</I>/</B>
</DIV>




<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt">Registered in Australia Rio Tinto Limited 120 Collins Street Melbourne 3000 Australia ABN 96
004 458 404
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto&#146;s integrated operations will be progressively upgraded through this sequence:
</DIV>

</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Brockman 4 Phase 2 project includes an expansion of the village, additional mine fleet
and construction of a primary crusher and a 4-kilometre overland conveyor to increase the
Brockman 4 operation from its scheduled 22 Mt/a to 40 Mt/a capacity in the first half of
2013.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Western Turner Syncline expansion incorporates the construction of a primary crusher
and a 20-kilometre overland conveyor to deliver ore to the Tom Price primary stockpiles.
Existing Tom Price infrastructure will be utilised, including the high grade and low grade
processing plants, stockyards, train load-out and on-site facilities. The first phase will
provide 15 Mt/a capacity from the second half of 2013.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Both developments will require a number of Government and regulatory approvals.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>About Rio Tinto</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto is a leading international mining group headquartered in the UK, combining
Rio Tinto plc, a London and NYSE listed company, and Rio Tinto Limited, which is listed
on the Australian Securities Exchange.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto&#146;s business is finding, mining, and processing mineral resources. Major products
are aluminium, copper, diamonds, energy (coal and uranium), gold, industrial minerals
(borax, titanium dioxide, salt, talc) and iron ore. Activities span the world but are
strongly represented in Australia and North America with significant businesses in South
America, Asia, Europe and southern Africa.
</DIV>

</DIV>

<!-- PAGEBREAK -->

<DIV style="font-family: Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif">



<P><DIV style="position: relative; float: left; width: 5%">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 30pt"><IMG src="u10286u1028600.gif" alt="(RIO TINTO LOGO)">
</DIV>

</DIV>
<DIV style="position: relative; float: right; width: 90%">

<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Exhibit&nbsp;99.2</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">120 Collins Street<BR>
Melbourne 3000<BR>
Australia<BR>
T &#043;61 (0)&nbsp;3 9283 3333<BR>
F &#043;61 (0)&nbsp;3 9283 3707

</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Press release
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Rio Tinto and Chinalco to form joint venture for exploration in China</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>3 December&nbsp;2010</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto and Chinalco today signed a non-binding Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)
to establish a landmark exploration joint venture (JV)&nbsp;in China.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The JV will explore mainland China for world-class mineral deposits and is expected to
come into operation in the first half of next year. It is intended that between three and
five large area exploration projects will be selected for initial focus by the JV, with
the potential for additional regions to be added at a later date.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Chinalco will hold a 51 per cent interest in the JV and Rio Tinto will hold a 49 per
cent interest.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto chief executive Tom Albanese said: &#147;This exploration JV is the latest chapter in
the rich history of partnerships between Rio Tinto and China. The combination of skills
provided by Rio Tinto and Chinalco offers great potential to unlock value for mutual
benefit.&#148;
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Chinalco president Xiong Weiping said: &#147;Against the backdrop of the globalisation of
resources supporting the globalisation of the world economy, for both sides to build on
our respective strengths and establish an exploration JV is a win-win measure that will
deepen our cooperation and meet the challenges of the market&#148;.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Mr Albanese and Mr Xiong attended a special MoU signing ceremony at the Diaoyutai State
Guesthouse in Beijing. Rio Tinto&#146;s Executive Committee, senior Chinalco executives and
Chinese Government officials were also present.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Chinalco&#146;s expertise and deep understanding of the Chinese environment will
complement Rio Tinto&#146;s application of world-leading technologies and experience in
operating global mining projects.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto will appoint the chief executive of the exploration JV, with the chairman of
the five-member Board nominated by Chinalco.
</DIV>


<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Cont...</I>/</B>
</DIV>



<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt">Registered in Australia Rio Tinto Limited 120 Collins Street Melbourne 3000 Australia ABN 96
004 458 404
</DIV>



</DIV>

    <TD align="left" valign="top">&nbsp;</TD>

    <TD align="right" valign="top">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR>
<!-- End Table Body -->
</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>About Rio Tinto</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto is a leading international mining group headquartered in the UK, combining
Rio Tinto plc, a London and NYSE listed company, and Rio Tinto Limited, which is listed
on the Australian Securities Exchange.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto&#146;s business is finding, mining, and processing mineral resources. Major products
are aluminium, copper, diamonds, energy (coal and uranium), gold, industrial minerals
(borax, titanium dioxide, salt, talc) and iron ore. Activities span the world but are
strongly represented in Australia and North America with significant businesses in South
America, Asia, Europe and southern Africa.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 30pt"><IMG src="u10286u1028600.gif" alt="(RIO TINTO LOGO)">
</DIV>

</DIV>
<DIV style="position: relative; float: right; width: 90%">



<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Exhibit&nbsp;99.3</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto plc<BR>
2 Eastbourne Terrace<BR>
London W2 6LG<BR>
United Kingdom<BR>
T &#043;44 (0)&nbsp;20 7781 2000<BR>
F &#043;44 (0)&nbsp;20 7781 1800

</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt">Press release
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>Rio Tinto announces modernisation and expansion of Canadian aluminium smelters</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>14 December&nbsp;2010</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto is to invest in its Canadian aluminium smelters to improve production efficiency
through modernisation and expansion. The bulk of this new investment &#151; US$758&nbsp;million &#151;
will be spent on completing the first phase of the AP60 plant in Saguenay&#150;Lac-Saint-Jean,
Quebec. Rio Tinto will also invest an additional US$300&nbsp;million for further construction
in preparation for the US$2.5&nbsp;billion modernisation of the Kitimat smelter in British
Columbia.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">AP technology, developed by Rio Tinto Alcan, is designed to improve energy efficiency and
reduce costs of aluminium production. AP60 is the latest generation of the bespoke
technology and metal output per pot at the plant will be 40 per cent higher than at
existing smelters.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Kitimat modernisation project will increase the smelter&#146;s current production capacity
by more than 48 per cent to approximately 420,000 tonnes per year. The modernised Kitimat
smelter will be powered exclusively by hydroelectricity and use Rio Tinto Alcan&#146;s
proprietary AP technology to reduce its emissions intensity by more than 50 per cent per
year.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Jacynthe C&#244;t&#233;, chief executive, Rio Tinto Alcan, said &#147;The first phase of the AP60 plant,
which will become the platform for future generations of our AP series, underlines Rio
Tinto Alcan&#146;s position as the world leader in aluminium smelting technologies. This
proprietary technology has already evolved from AP50 to AP60 since this project was first
announced. It is the industry benchmark &#151; the most cost-effective, energy-efficient, and
environmentally-friendly smelting technology commercially available.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&#147;The modernisation of our Kitimat smelter is truly a transformational project, in line
with our strategic objective to grow via long-life, large-scale, low-cost assets. Once
completed, Kitimat will be one of the lowest-cost smelters in the world.&#148;
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The first phase of the AP60 plant will have 38 pots and an annual production capacity of
60,000 tonnes of aluminium by 2013. This initial step will also include the
infrastructure required for the subsequent phases, which would bring the total production
capacity to 460,000 tonnes, powered by clean, renewable hydroelectricity.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto is expected to have spent approximately US$371&nbsp;million on the AP60 project by the
end of the year. Rio Tinto is also expected to have spent approximately US$350&nbsp;million on
the Kitimat modernisation project, for which final approval is expected in 2011.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto&#146;s continued investment in these projects is consistent with the modernisation
strategy that was set out following the acquisition of Alcan and is in-keeping with the
Group&#146;s 2007 commitments to the governments of Canada and Quebec.
</DIV>

</DIV>
<BR clear="all"><BR>

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->&nbsp;<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<P><HR noshade><P>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><IMG src="u10286u1028600.gif" alt="(RIO TINTO LOGO)">
</DIV>

</DIV>
<DIV style="position: relative; float: right; width: 90%">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Notes to editors</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">AP60 technology was first developed at Rio Tinto Alcan&#146;s research and development
facilities in the Rhone-Alpes region of France. When Phase 1 of the
plant becomes operational, the Arvida Research and Development Centre in Jonqui&#232;re, Quebec
will lead ongoing activities towards commercialising AP60 technology. It will also be
supported by research and development teams in Voreppe and Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne, France.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">AP60 is the next step in Rio Tinto Alcan&#146;s suite of industry benchmark smelting
technologies. AP60 will operate at an exceptional 600 kilo amperes (kA), which
represents a 100 kilo ampere step change from AP50 technology. Like all AP series
technologies, AP60 is focussed on productivity and reduction of full economic cost of
production.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>About Rio Tinto</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto is a leading international mining group headquartered in the UK, combining
Rio Tinto plc, a London and NYSE listed company, and Rio Tinto Limited, which is listed
on the Australian Securities Exchange.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto&#146;s business is finding, mining, and processing mineral resources. Major products
are aluminium, copper, diamonds, energy (coal and uranium), gold, industrial minerals
(borax, titanium dioxide, salt, talc) and iron ore. Activities span the world but are
strongly represented in Australia and North America with significant businesses in South
America, Asia, Europe and southern Africa.
</DIV>

<P><DIV style="position: relative; float: left; width: 5%">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 30pt"><IMG src="u10286u1028600.gif" alt="(RIO TINTO LOGO)">
</DIV>

</DIV>
<DIV style="position: relative; float: right; width: 90%">


<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Exhibit&nbsp;99.4</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto plc<BR>
2 Eastbourne Terrace<BR>
London W2 6LG<BR>
United Kingdom<BR>
T &#043;44 (0)&nbsp;20 7781 2000<BR>
F &#043;44 (0)&nbsp;20 7781 1800

</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Press release
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>Rio Tinto announces the pricing of the secondary public offering of
25,600,000 shares of Cloud Peak Energy Inc.</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>16 December&nbsp;2010</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto announced today the pricing of the underwritten secondary offering of 25,600,000
shares of Cloud Peak Energy Inc.&#146;s common stock for US$19.50 per share. Following the
completion of the offering, Rio Tinto will retain an approximately 6.2 per cent interest
in Cloud Peak Energy Resources LLC (assuming no exercise of the underwriters&#146;
overallotment option). Subject to closing, the transaction is expected to generate gross
proceeds of US$499.2&nbsp;million. The transaction is expected to close on or about 21 December
2010. The underwriters have an over-allotment option to purchase up to 3,800,000
additional shares of Cloud Peak Energy Inc.&#146;s common stock, exercisable within the next 30
days, and if exercised, would be expected to generate an additional US$74.1&nbsp;million of
gross proceeds.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">If the overallotment is fully exercised, this offering would result in the divestment of
100 per cent of Rio Tinto&#146;s holdings in Cloud Peak Energy. The Tax Receivable Agreement
entered into between Cloud Peak Energy Inc. and Rio Tinto in connection with the initial
public offering in November&nbsp;2009 will remain in effect.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&#147;The pricing of the secondary offering demonstrates another successful outcome of our
overall divestment strategy,&#148; said Guy Elliott, Chief Financial Officer, Rio Tinto. &#147;With
the proceeds from the Cloud Peak Energy transactions and the sale of Jacobs Ranch, the
total gross proceeds for the divestment of the majority of Rio Tinto Energy America will be
at least US$2.0&nbsp;billion.&#148;
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The offering of these securities will be made by means of a prospectus supplement and
accompanying prospectus, forming an effective part of the registration statement, copies
of which may be obtained from the joint book-running managers, Credit Suisse Securities
(USA)&nbsp;LLC at One Madison Avenue 1B, New York, New York 10010, Attention: Prospectus
Department or by calling (800)&nbsp;221-1037; Morgan Stanley &#038; Co. Incorporated at 180 Varick
Street, 2nd Floor, New York, New York 10014, Attention: Prospectus Department or by
calling (866)&nbsp;718-1649 or by emailing: prospectus@morganstanley.com; RBC Capital Markets,
LLC at Three World Financial Center, 200 Vesey Street, 8th Floor, New York, NY 10281-8098,
Attention: Equity Syndicate or by calling (212)&nbsp;428-6670; or J.P. Morgan Securities LLC,
c/o Broadridge Financial Solutions, 1155 Long Island Avenue, Edgewood, New York 11717 or
by calling (866)&nbsp;803-9204.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">A shelf registration statement relating to the offering of the common shares has
previously been filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and has become
effective. This press release shall not constitute an offer to sell or a solicitation of
an offer to buy, nor shall there be any sale of these securities in any state or
jurisdiction in which such an offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful prior to
registration or qualification under the securities laws of any such state or
jurisdiction.
</DIV>


<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Cont...</I>/</B>
</DIV>

</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>About Rio Tinto</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto is a leading international mining group headquartered in the UK, combining
Rio Tinto plc, a London and NYSE listed company, and Rio Tinto Limited, which is listed
on the Australian Securities Exchange.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto&#146;s business is finding, mining, and processing mineral resources. Major products
are aluminium, copper, diamonds, energy (coal and uranium), gold, industrial minerals
(borax, titanium dioxide, salt, talc) and iron ore. Activities span the world but are
strongly represented in Australia and North America with significant businesses in South
America, Asia, Europe and southern Africa.
</DIV>

<P><DIV style="position: relative; float: left; width: 5%">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 30pt"><IMG src="u10286u1028600.gif" alt="(RIO TINTO LOGO)">

<DIV style="position: relative; float: right; width: 90%">


<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Exhibit&nbsp;99.5</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto plc<BR>
2 Eastbourne Terrace<BR>
London W2 6LG<BR>
United Kingdom<BR>
T &#043;44 (0)&nbsp;20 7781 2000<BR>
F &#043;44 (0)&nbsp;20 7781 1800

</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt">Press release
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>Rio Tinto completes 100 per cent divestment of Cloud Peak Energy with fully
exercised over allotment</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>22 December&nbsp;2010</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto has completed a 100 per cent divestment of its equity holdings in Cloud Peak
Energy Inc. through a fully exercised over allotment in connection with a recently
announced secondary offering. Underwriters exercised their option to purchase 3,800,000
additional shares of Cloud Peak Energy Inc&#146;s common stock for US$19.50 per share. The
secondary offering of 25,600,000 shares and the over allotment closed on 21 December&nbsp;2010.
Gross proceeds from the over allotment were US$74.1&nbsp;million, bringing the total gross
proceeds from the secondary offering to US$573.3&nbsp;million.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto continues to have certain rights under the tax receivable agreement entered
into with Cloud Peak at the time of the initial public offering.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>About Rio Tinto</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto is a leading international mining group headquartered in the UK, combining
Rio Tinto plc, a London and NYSE listed company, and Rio Tinto Limited, which is listed
on the Australian Securities Exchange.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto&#146;s business is finding, mining, and processing mineral resources. Major products
are aluminium, copper, diamonds, energy (coal and uranium), gold, industrial minerals
(borax, titanium dioxide, salt, talc) and iron ore. Activities span the world but are
strongly represented in Australia and North America with significant businesses in South
America, Asia, Europe and southern Africa.
</DIV>


<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Cont...</I>/</B>
</DIV>

</DIV>

<DOCUMENT>
<TYPE>EX-99.6
<SEQUENCE>7
<FILENAME>u10286exv99w6.htm
<DESCRIPTION>EX-99.6
<TEXT>
<HTML>
<HEAD>
<TITLE>exv99w6</TITLE>
</HEAD>
<BODY bgcolor="#FFFFFF">
<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<DIV style="font-family: Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif">

<P><DIV style="position: relative; float: left; width: 5%">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 30pt"><IMG src="u10286u1028600.gif" alt="(LOGO)">
</DIV>

</DIV>
<DIV style="position: relative; float: right; width: 92%">

<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Exhibit&nbsp;99.6</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">120 Collins Street<BR>
Melbourne 3000<BR>
Australia<BR>
T &#043;61 (0)&nbsp;3 9283 3333<BR>
F &#043;61 (0)&nbsp;3 9283 3707

</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt">Press Release
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>Recommended A$16 per share cash offer by Rio Tinto for Riversdale</B>

</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>23 December&nbsp;2010</B>

</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Recommended cash offer price of A$16 per ordinary share values Riversdale at
approximately A$3.9&nbsp;billion<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">1</SUP>.</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Rio Tinto has entered into pre-bid agreements in relation to 14.9 per cent
of Riversdale&#146;s current shares on issue.</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Shareholders who have signed pre-bid agreements include a number of senior
executives of Riversdale including Michael O&#146;Keeffe (executive chairman), Steve
Mallyon (managing director) and Niall Lenahan (chief financial officer).</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Rio Tinto&#146;s offer provides Riversdale shareholders with an attractive,
all-cash offer for their shares at a substantial premium to historical trading
prices.</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Acquisition provides Rio Tinto with a substantial tier one coking coal
development pipeline in the emerging Moatize Basin in Mozambique, in line with Rio
Tinto&#146;s strategy of developing large, long-life, low operating cost assets to grow
shareholder value.</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto Group (LSE: RIO, ASX: RIO, NYSE: RIO) (&#147;Rio Tinto&#148;) and Riversdale Mining Limited
(ASX: RIV) (&#147;Riversdale&#148;) have entered into a Bid Implementation Agreement (&#147;BIA&#148;) for a
cash offer (the &#147;Offer&#148;) by Rio Tinto<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">2</SUP> to acquire all of the issued and
outstanding shares of Riversdale by way of a recommended off-market takeover offer.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Offer price of A$16 per share values Riversdale at approximately A$3.9
billion<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">3</SUP>. The Offer price represents a 46 per cent premium to the one-month volume
weighted average price (&#147;VWAP&#148;) of Riversdale shares to 3 November&nbsp;2010<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">4 </SUP>and a 24
per cent premium to the one-month VWAP of Riversdale shares to 3 December&nbsp;2010<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">5</SUP>.
The Offer will be financed through Rio Tinto&#146;s existing cash reserves and credit facilities.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Riversdale Directors<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">6</SUP> have recommended, in the absence of a superior proposal,
that shareholders accept Rio Tinto&#146;s Offer and have indicated they intend to accept the Offer
for shares in Riversdale which they control. Riversdale&#146;s executive chairman (Michael
O&#146;Keeffe), managing director (Steve Mallyon) and chief financial officer (Niall Lenahan) have
entered into pre-bid agreements in relation to shares in which they have a relevant interest.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">In aggregate, Rio Tinto has secured pre-bid agreements in relation to 14.9 per cent of
Riversdale&#146;s current shares on issue.
</DIV>


<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Cont...</I>/</B>
</DIV>



<DIV align="left">
<DIV style="font-size: 3pt; margin-top: 16pt; width: 18%; border-top: 1px solid #000000">&nbsp;</DIV>
</DIV>

<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">
<TR>
    <TD width="3%"></TD>
    <TD width="1%"></TD>
    <TD width="96%"></TD>
</TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left"><SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">1</SUP></TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>On a fully diluted basis.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left"><SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">2</SUP></TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>The offer is likely to be made by a wholly owned subsidiary of Rio Tinto.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">

<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always">&nbsp;</H5><P>

<DIV style="font-family: Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif">
<P><DIV style="position: relative; float: left; width: 5%">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><IMG src="u10286u1028600.gif" alt="(LOGO)">
</DIV>

</DIV>
<DIV style="position: relative; float: right; width: 92%">
<DIV align="center">
<TABLE style="font-size: 10pt" cellspacing="0" border="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">

<!-- End Table Body -->

</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Doug Ritchie, Rio Tinto chief executive Energy said: &#147;The acquisition of Riversdale is in
line with our growth strategy of investing in, developing and operating large, long term,
cost-competitive mines and businesses driven by the quality of each opportunity.&#148;
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&#147;Rio Tinto&#146;s extensive experience in infrastructure and large project development combined
with our significant financial capacity means that we are well placed to take Riversdale&#146;s
asset base through its next phase of development. We believe Rio Tinto is one of the few
groups in the world with the capabilities, values and incentives to develop the projects
quickly and to a world-class standard, bringing considerable benefit to the people of
Mozambique,&#148; Mr Ritchie said.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&#147;This investment underlines Rio Tinto&#146;s commitment to Africa. Our reach extends beyond our
operating mines to include an extensive exploration programme and numerous active projects in
the region.&#148;
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Implementation</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto and Riversdale have entered into a Bid Implementation Agreement in respect of the
Offer. A copy of the BIA is attached to Riversdale&#146;s announcement of the Offer.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Offer is subject to a number of conditions including Rio Tinto acquiring a relevant
interest in excess of 50 per cent in Riversdale, Foreign Investment Review Board approval as
well as no material adverse change occurring and Riversdale conducting its business within
certain specified parameters. A full list of the conditions to the Offer is set out in
Appendix&nbsp;I<I>.</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The BIA also contains customary deal protection mechanisms including &#147;no shop&#148; and &#147;no
talk&#148; restrictions and a matching right for Rio Tinto in the event of a competing
proposal. A break fee of A$37.8&nbsp;million is also payable to Rio Tinto in certain
circumstances.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Next Steps</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto and Riversdale expect to dispatch the Bidder&#146;s Statement and Target&#146;s
Statement in relation to the Offer in January&nbsp;2011.
</DIV>

</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>About Rio Tinto</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto is a leading international mining group headquartered in the UK, combining
Rio Tinto plc, a London and NYSE listed company, and Rio Tinto Limited, which is listed on
the Australian Securities Exchange.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto&#146;s business is finding, mining, and processing mineral resources. Major products are
aluminium, copper, diamonds, energy (coal and uranium), gold, industrial minerals (borax,
titanium dioxide, salt, talc) and iron ore. Activities span the world but are strongly
represented in Australia and North America with significant businesses in South America,
Asia, Europe and southern Africa.
</DIV>

<DIV align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 18pt"><B>Appendix&nbsp;I</B>
</DIV>


<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left"><B>1.</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><B>Conditions to the Offer</B></TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>The Offer, and any contract resulting from the acceptance of the Offer, are
subject to the following conditions:</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="4%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left"><B>(a)</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><B>Minimum acceptance condition</B></TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="4%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Before the end of the Offer Period, Rio Tinto Group and its Related Entities
have relevant interests in excess of 50% of Riversdale Shares then on issue.</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="4%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left"><B>(b)</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><B>FIRB approval</B></TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="4%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>One of the following occurs before the end of the Offer Period:</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="8%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">(i)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Rio Tinto receives a notice from the Treasurer of the Commonwealth of Australia
(<B>Treasurer</B>) or his agent to the effect that there is no objection to the acquisition of
the Riversdale Shares by Rio Tinto or another wholly owned member of the Rio Tinto Group
(by any means permitted by the Corporations Act) under the Commonwealth Government&#146;s
foreign investment policy, such notice being unconditional;</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="8%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">(ii)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>the period provided under the <I>Foreign Acquisitions and Takeovers Act 1975</I>
(Cth) (as amended) (<B>FATA</B>) during which the Treasurer may make an order under
section 22 of the FATA prohibiting the acquisition of Riversdale Shares by Rio
Tinto or another wholly owned member of the Rio Tinto Group (by any means
permitted under the Corporations Act) has elapsed, without such an order being
made; or</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="8%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">(iii)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>if an interim order prohibiting such acquisition is made, the subsequent
period for making a final order prohibiting the acquisition of Riversdale Shares
by Rio Tinto or another wholly owned member of the Rio Tinto Group has elapsed,
without such final order being made.</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="4%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left"><B>(c)</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><B>No material adverse event</B></TD>
</TR>

out in the renewal application forms or otherwise disclosed by Riversdale
to Rio Tinto before the Announcement Date.

the acquisition of Riversdale Shares) or requires the divestiture of any assets
of the Riversdale Group or the Rio Tinto Group.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="4%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left"><B>(j)</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><B>Non-existence or exercise of certain rights</B></TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>

    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Between the Announcement Date and the end of the Offer Period, there is no person
(other than a member of the Rio Tinto Group) having any rights, being entitled to
or exercising any rights, alleging an entitlement, or expressing or announcing an
intention (whether or not that intention is stated to be a final or determined
decision of that person) and in all cases whether subject to conditions or not,
as a result of any change of control event in respect of Riversdale (including
Rio Tinto acquiring shares in Riversdale) or any of its subsidiaries or assets,
to:</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">

    <TD width="3%" nowrap align="left">(i)</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>

Project Approval to which Riversdale or any of its subsidiaries is a party (for
this purpose an alteration includes, without limitation, an alteration of the
operations of a Mining Interest, material contract or material Project Approval,

or applicable to the Mining Interest, contract or Project Approval);</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">

venture (incorporated or unincorporated); or</TD>

</TR>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt">Press release
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>Weather impacts Rio Tinto Coal Australia&#146;s Queensland operations</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>29 December&nbsp;2010</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">As a result of severe monsoonal rain in central and northern Queensland, <I>force majeure </I>has
been declared on coal sales contracts from mines in which Rio Tinto Coal Australia has a
majority interest. The mines are Hail Creek, Kestrel, Blair Athol and Clermont in
Queensland&#146;s Bowen Basin.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The severe monsoonal rain, on top of the significant rainfalls in November and December, has
had an adverse impact on mining operations, and has cut access roads and rail networks.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">As rain is continuing to fall in the region and further rains are forecast, Rio Tinto Coal
Australia is currently unable to provide an estimate of the full impact of this adverse
weather or the duration of the f<I>orce majeure </I>declaration.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">While all efforts are being made to minimise the impact of this adverse weather on coal
production, our primary focus at this time is on the safety and well-being of our employees
and their families.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>About Rio Tinto</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto is a leading international mining group headquartered in the UK, combining
Rio Tinto plc, a London and NYSE listed company, and Rio Tinto Limited, which is listed on
the Australian Securities Exchange.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto&#146;s business is finding, mining, and processing mineral resources. Major products
are aluminium, copper, diamonds, energy (coal and uranium), gold, industrial minerals
(borax, titanium dioxide, salt, talc) and iron ore. Activities span the world but are
strongly represented in Australia and North America with significant businesses in South
America, Asia, Europe and southern Africa.
</DIV>


<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Cont...</I>/</B>
</DIV>


</DIV>
